summary: A 100-foot Wisconsin standard tower built in 1939 near the village of Friendship, staffed each spring fire season until the state decommissioned its lookout network in 2015.

facts.design: Wisconsin standard tower, 100 ft, external protected ladder

access.note: No source found describing public access or a maintained trail; treat as unstaffed DNR infrastructure, not a confirmed open climb.

events.note: Built December 1939 as a Wisconsin standard 100-foot tower
Staffed intermittently each spring fire season until Wisconsin decommissioned its lookout network in 2015
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, December 6, 2017, as US 1259, WI 45

evidence.supports: built December 1939, 100-foot Wisconsin standard tower with external protected ladder
evidence.quote: Friendship, also historically called Skyline, is a 100-foot Wisconsin standard tower featuring an external protected ladder. It was built in December 1939.

evidence.supports: staffed intermittently each spring until 2015 decommissioning
evidence.quote: Friendship tower was staffed intermittently during spring fire season until 2015 when Wisconsin decommissioned its lookout network.

evidence.supports: tower still standing per FFLA Wisconsin list
evidence.quote: Friendship Mound (Skyline) Adams 43.98731 -89.81813 Tower Standing NHLR US 1259, WI 45

notes_for_editor: Searched for a local/CCC construction story (Adams County Historical Society 'Friendship Sesquicentennial' page) but it discusses Friendship Mound's sheriff's radio tower and a lighted star, not the fire lookout, and has no bearing on this record; not cited. No source found on who built it, current public access, or whether it is climbable, so those fields are left unknown rather than guessed. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed several story sentences that went beyond the cited source (an invented etymology for the 'Skyline' name, a claim the design was 'widely used' by the state forestry service, invented reasoning about dry grass/wind/debris burning driving spring staffing, and an invented claim that decommissioning was 'in favor of aircraft and other detection methods') — none of this appears in the NHLR page text. Also note cite 2's FFLA list spells the feature 'Friendship Mound (Skyline)', slightly differing from cite 1's 'Friendship (Skyline)'; not treated as a correction since both clearly refer to the same tower.
